380.t: New songs and a tuba ensemble piece for New York
380.s: He mentions a new lyric by Mary Lou, plans to push his songs, and pieces for tubas sent to Bob Stewart and Howard Johnson.
380.ch: Billy Berg's, Granz and Nat Cole
380.q: Yeah. I'm in love with it. It's really a great lyric. And also another thing, "Birds On the Wing," which I am hoping to get to Ella or Sarah. I think they might like that one. I've been writing songs most of my life, but I've been a little too shy to push them, except some of those that people just…

380.t: The composing grant and the work Jazz Travels
380.s: He is writing every day on a piece called Jazz Travels, including a finished "Merry-Go-Round" with Mary Lou's lyric.
380.q: Well, my original title for the whole work is Jazz Travels, which, you know, can cover everything, because Jazz does travel. It has to travel to exist! So one thing I've completed is a thing called "Merry-Go-Round." I just took it to a professional copyist. I'll give you a copy. Today he brought it…

607.t: Miss English blog and grammar musical
607.s: Her Miss English pet-peeves blog and the musical 'The Grammarians' with Nan Schwartz.
607.q: Well I haven’t updated it in a long time because I feel as if maybe it is dated. I know so many people now who are upset at apostrophes being used to pluralize. Somebody posted about it on FaceBook just the other day. I forget what kind of a store it was but let’s say it was Waymans and then it…

1022.t: Future plans and how he writes tunes
1022.s: He hopes to write more, mentions a strings record, and describes composing from the piano and trumpet.
1022.ch: Playing fast, best gigs and the future
1022.q: Well hopefully exactly what I’m doing now, with the exception of maybe writing more for hire. Hopefully, I just did a strings record, a record with strings, six different strings, and I didn’t do the string writing but the tunes are mine, the songs are mine, some of the songs are mine. Some are…

840.t: Composing, a possible leader record and the Hal Leonard bass book
840.s: He writes mostly for projects, hopes to record on Azica with Joey Baron and Kenny Barron, and has a walking bass line book coming from Hal Leonard.
840.q: MB: No, Kenny Barron is the piano player, and I want to use Kenny too. I want to use Kenny. I haven’t called Kenny about it, but I talked to Joey a little bit about it, and he’s interested. And Peter Sprague, this guitar player I think and do a quartet thing. So that looks like it might happen. Hal…

328.t: How much he has written and unperformed pieces
328.s: He has written too many pieces and a piece for Chick Corea is being copied.
328.ch: Europe years and the return home
328.q: There must have been a couple of pieces. I know one piece I wrote for Chick Corea, and it just – with a large ensemble. It was a big band with two french horns and a tuba, and I guess there was maybe a four or five rhythm section. Now somebody – I just sent it to someone last week. They’re going to…

576.t: Writing lyrics for Don Cherry's Remembrance
576.s: Rediscovering the heavy lyrics she wrote, she doubts she wrote them.
576.q: But I, but, you know, and then I found them… I guess I still have them over there. I thought I didn‟t have them, but if found them one day when you were here. We were rehearsing. Brown, C.: Yes.

589.t: The text and movements of Colors
589.s: The text is in the program, not sung, and Lewis cannot recall the movement titles.
589.q: Yes, that I don’t remember. You write something, and you wrote it, and then you move on. If I had known that you wanted it this moment, I would have gotten it and had it available.

555.t: A trumpet, trombone and strings piece for Susan Slaughter
555.s: She is composing, and repeatedly revising, her first piece for trombone, trumpet and strings as thanks for the horn Susan Slaughter sent.
555.q: Not in the way that people think. I think about it and think about it and think about it before I write. I was writing, before my eyes got bad, a thing for the trumpet player and trombone player that sent me the horn, because I’ve got to send them something, so I was writing for them. Every time .…

672.t: Songs as high points of songwriting
672.s: She tries to name great lyrics, recalling Over the Weekend and Lush Life songs.
672.q: Okay. I remember there’s a song that Johnny Mathis did, and I did it. It was a great song. But I can’t remember right now. Oh well. Over the Weekend.

614.t: Andy LaVerne's writing and Chuck Mangione as a potential writer
614.s: Wong asks about a former band writer; Herman plans to ask Chuck Mangione to write for the band.
614.q: Yeah, that's right, I think he would -- this is off the record, completely, but (unintelligible) people that, if he went back to school now he could really help himself.

454.t: Symphonies and string quartets he never got to; nothing fully worked
454.s: He always wanted to write five-movement symphonies and quartets; no piece came out as he wanted and the new Atlantic balance is wrong.
454.q: I've always wanted to do symphonies. But the last three or four years, I've just lost the energy, man.

75.t: The suite "Hills of New York" and composing
75.s: He is still working on the suite and says he is not a real songwriter.
75.ch: Closing: recent career, family and travel
75.q: : I have been sidetracked several times. You know, with my lifestyle, sometimes things get... I do a lot of traveling. I don't stay in one place too long. This is the first time, around now, that I've been sitting in one place. I don't know, I've wanted to sit down to serious writing many times,…
